facts.statement: SimpleImputer learns one replacement value per feature from the data passed to fit, with strategies including mean, median, most_frequent and constant.
Use SimpleImputer(strategy=declared_strategy).fit(X_train), then call transform(X_validation) without fitting on validation rows.
Inspect statistics_ to check the fitted replacement values and verify they remain unchanged after validation transformation.
Compute the arithmetic mean with np.mean(numeric_values, axis=0), so each selected numeric feature column is summarized over rows.

Compute standard deviation with np.std(numeric_values, axis=0, ddof=0), which divides squared deviations by N before taking the square root; use ddof=1 only when the stated calculation requires the N−1 divisor.
Write assert predicate checks for the declared valid, boundary and failure cases; a false predicate raises AssertionError during ordinary non-optimized execution.

practice.objective: Within supplied infrastructure scaffolding, write the required imports and a Python function that fits one SimpleImputer on training distance values using the declared mean strategy, then reuses it on validation distance values. Compute the mean and population standard deviation of the observed training distances, and author assertions for valid, boundary and deliberately incorrect results.
practice.success: Observed training distances 2 and 6 produce a columnwise mean of 4 and population standard deviation of 2. Validation distance 100 remains 100, and a missing validation distance becomes 4. A validation input consisting of one missing distance also becomes 4. Assertions verify these outputs and unchanged statistics_ after both transformations. A deliberately incorrect expected replacement fails an assertion under ordinary non-optimized execution.

live_code.required_skill: Implement training-only imputer fitting, reuse its fitted state, compute columnwise numerical summaries, and assert output and state invariants in a learner-defined function.
live_code.starter_state_intent: Supply only distance fixtures, the declared mean strategy, a function interface and an assertion-checking harness—not complete implementation code. X_train contains distances 2, 6 and a missing value; numeric_values contains only the observed training distances as a two-dimensional, one-column array. X_validation contains distance 100 and a missing value. Supply a separate one-row missing-distance boundary input and an intentionally incorrect expected replacement for the failure check.
live_code.observable_success: The learner-written function imports its dependencies, fits exactly one imputer using X_train only, and transforms both validation fixtures without refitting. Returned summaries are mean 4 and population standard deviation 2. Returned transformed distances preserve 100 and replace missing entries with 4. Learner-written assertions compare copied statistics_ with the state after each transformation; the supplied harness observes AssertionError for the deliberately false check.
